skill.description: Reusable MCP server development patterns for Python projects, including async tool handlers, database backends, caching, rate limiting, validation, and test examples.
skill.summary: Build reusable Python MCP servers with async tools, database integration, and testing patterns.
skill.author: Azeem-2

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, Python import syntax, placeholder database configuration, and variable names such as db or id. The review did find high-risk semantic issues in the example patterns: raw SQL construction with dynamic identifiers and permissive authorization defaults. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed SKILL.md text.

remediation.issue: Raw SQL strings interpolate table names, fields, order clauses, and limits.
remediation.suggestion: Use SQLAlchemy expression builders or strict allowlists for identifiers, sort fields, and numeric clauses before executing queries.

remediation.issue: The default permission hook returns true and identity is read from tool arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Require authenticated identity from trusted MCP context and implement deny-by-default permission checks before registering CRUD tools.

remediation.issue: Examples include placeholder database credentials and environment defaults.
remediation.suggestion: Remove default credentials from examples and document required secret-managed configuration for REDIS_URL and DATABASE_URL.

semantic_findings.title: Unsafe Raw SQL Construction in Examples
semantic_findings.description: The examples build SQL strings by interpolating table names, column names, sort clauses, and limits. Parameter binding is used for values, but identifiers and clauses still need allowlists or query-builder APIs.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Multiple helper methods concatenate dynamic identifiers and clauses into SQL. This is a clear injection-prone pattern if any table, field, sort, or limit input is attacker controlled.

semantic_findings.title: Authorization Defaults Allow Broad Access
semantic_findings.description: The default permission method always returns true, while caller-supplied user context controls identity fields. This can disable user scoping in generated CRUD tools unless implementers replace the stub.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code extracts user_id from tool arguments and the permission hook returns true by default. The surrounding CRUD filters rely on that hook, so generated tools can omit tenant scoping.

content.user_title: Build MCP Servers with Reusable Patterns
content.value_statement: Teams need reliable patterns for exposing backend operations to AI agents through MCP. This skill provides reusable Python structures for tools, storage, validation, caching, and tests.
actual_capabilities: Defines a reusable BaseMCPServer pattern for registering and calling MCP tools.
Shows async database adapter patterns for PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Redis, and SQLAlchemy.
Includes generic CRUD and bulk operation tool patterns for entity-based APIs.
Demonstrates a task management MCP server built from the shared patterns.
Provides pytest-style testing examples with mock database managers.
limitations: The skill is documentation and example code, not a packaged runnable server.
Security controls are illustrative and need production hardening before deployment.
Database schemas, migrations, authentication, and hosting are left to the implementer.
Examples assume Python and common async database libraries.

use_cases.title: Create Internal MCP Tools
use_cases.description: Build a server that exposes approved internal operations to AI agents through MCP tools.

use_cases.title: Prototype Database-backed Agents
use_cases.description: Use the CRUD patterns to test how an agent can safely read and update domain records.

use_cases.title: Standardize MCP Server Tests
use_cases.description: Adapt the mock database and pytest examples to verify tool behavior before deployment.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Basic Server
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new MCP project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the mcp-server skill to outline a simple Python MCP server for my domain. Include tools, inputs, and storage needs.

prompt_templates.title: Design CRUD Tools
prompt_templates.scenario: Create entity operations from a domain model.
prompt_templates.prompt: Using the mcp-server patterns, design CRUD MCP tools for this entity model: [describe fields]. Include validation and user scoping.

prompt_templates.title: Add Storage Backends
prompt_templates.scenario: Connect an MCP server to a database.
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply the mcp-server database patterns to support PostgreSQL for this MCP server. Include connection setup, transactions, and safe query practices.

prompt_templates.title: Review Production Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my MCP server design against the mcp-server skill. Focus on authorization, SQL safety, rate limits, caching, error handling, and tests.

output_examples.input: I need an MCP server for project tasks.
output_examples.output: A structured server design with create, get, list, update, delete, and search tools, plus validation and storage recommendations.

output_examples.input: Add database support to my MCP tool server.
output_examples.output: A backend plan covering connection lifecycle, transaction boundaries, supported database choices, and safe parameter handling.

output_examples.input: How should I test these MCP tools?
output_examples.output: A focused test plan with mock storage, success cases, validation failures, permission cases, and end-to-end tool calls.

best_practices: Replace illustrative permission checks with real authentication and authorization before deployment.
Use allowlisted identifiers or query builders when generating database queries.
Keep secrets in managed environment configuration and avoid hardcoded default credentials.
anti_patterns: Do not expose generic CRUD tools without strict entity, field, and permission boundaries.
Do not concatenate user-controlled table names, columns, sort fields, or limits into SQL.
Do not treat sample rate limits and caching settings as production defaults without review.

faq.question: Is this a complete MCP server package?
faq.answer: No. It is a documentation skill with reusable patterns and example code for building your own server.

faq.question: Which language do the examples use?
faq.answer: The examples use Python with async MCP, database, caching, and testing libraries.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Does it handle authentication for me?
faq.answer: No. The examples show where permission checks belong, but production authentication must be implemented separately.

faq.question: Does it support multiple databases?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples discuss PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Redis caching, and SQLAlchemy-style adapters.

faq.question: What should I review before using the examples?
faq.answer: Review authorization, SQL query construction, secret handling, rate limits, logging, and deployment settings.
